While this would be useful. GIFs are horribly wasteful in bandwidth.

I prefer to make WebMs. While not as universally supported by websites, they have controls, allow audio, and are much smaller bandwidth wise.

This is the tool I use. It's fairly simple. 1080p 15 second long WebMs are like 1-5 MB depending on content. A similar GIF would look horrible and still take up a lot more space.

Gfycat supports webms, and imgur converts gifs into webms (just change the extension to either .webm or .gifv), but doesn't support direct uploads of .webms (you have to upload a .gif and it will convert it automatically), so doesn't support audio.

I got my original Pi ages ago, overclocked the hell out of it and set it up as a multi-boot media center / torrent box.

When the pi2 came out, there was no availability and my desire to get one kinda fizzled. Should I get one now, or have competing boards made themselves too attractive?
Had a Pi for ages, but never got a Pi 2 (of no availability). Should I? Or are there other boards I should be looking at?
Good question, I'd like to here everyone's opinion also. I have an old pi I use for SNES and a media server. It would be nice to buy the new one or another type of board for another project.

I never had a Pi 1 but I love my Pi 2. Overclocked mine and I get great PSX performance and mostly good N64 performance. I don't know if you'd benefit from one for what you're doing but if you're into emulation I'd recommend it. RetroPie is awesome.

I would rather have an Odroid C1. It's got a 1.5GHz quad core processor, (overclockable to 1.7GHz) 1GB of RAM, gigabit Ethernet and a built in IR receiver. All for about $35

One thing I didn't like about the raspberry pi is that the Ethernet and USB ports were on the same bus which created a bottleneck if you were to use an external HDD along with Ethernet. The new model might be different though.

Had a Pi1, and had a lot of fun with it... programmed it, overclocked it, popped it (still don't know how). I really liked the plucky little board, but I thought it was a bit sensitive and weak so i decided to hold off for the V2.

By comparison, the V2 is a TANK. WAY more powerful CPU, more GPIO (than the original v1), MicroSD slot (HATED the big SD slot, it was extremely loose on mine) and a lot more durable. I've had one that's been running continuously for nearly 6 months with only a few reboots and it just keeps trucking along. You can even run a proper ARMv7 OS like Ubuntu, FreeBSD, or (possibly soon) Red Hat.

tl;dr - Pi2 all the way

I had a Pi 1 for a couple of years, using it daily as a home server. Got the Pi 2 earlier this year as a replacement. The difference is night and day! The Pi 2 is as capable as a full desktop system a decade ago, but at a fraction of the cost and power usage.

The BeagleBone Black is a nice alternative if you want to have more IO on board. However the community has appeared to fizzle. I own both as well as some Arduino boards. There is a lot of info and websites dedicated to the Pi so for pure quantity of available info for that platform the Pi would be my choice.
